packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 18 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure / rule statement
No identification of work or author was present in my context before reading, and I make none. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..008 in this packet directory. One thing beyond the letter of the rules: I ran a file listing of the two packet directories named to me (to see the image filenames); that showed that packet.json exists but I did not open it.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview of the inside of a wooden book board with leather turn-ins, a pasted paper slip half hidden by a colour target, and, along the lower (spine-side) edge, a horizontal parchment strip used as a binding reinforcement. The strip carries script running parallel to its long edge, upright in the image as supplied.
- The strip shows two columns of text separated by an intercolumn with a vertical ruled double line (visible in image-003). Four lines of each column survive; the top line sits directly under the cut edge, the fourth line is on the lower edge next to the joint. No running title, no rubric, no enlarged or coloured initial, no underlining, no interlinear or marginal gloss visible. One tiny red speck above line 3 of the left column (image-003/004) may be pigment or offset; not readable as a letter.
- Script: a formal book hand, brown ink, with superscript abbreviation strokes (d' , and'n, kein'), round-s and long-s, z with a tail. Language is a German vernacular (observation from the word forms, not an identification).
- Lines 3 and partly 4 of both columns are covered by adhering white fibrous paper/pastedown remains, and the left end of the left column is torn away and covered.
- image-005: overview of the second face: another board (or the other side) with a parchment strip along the upper edge. This strip shows ruling (vertical and horizontal lines) but NO legible script on the exposed side; only a few dark specks (image-007, image-008) that I cannot resolve into letters.
- Tentative interpretation only: the strip is a horizontal slice across a two-column leaf, so each column gives four consecutive lines but the two columns are not continuous with each other (an unknown number of lines is lost between the end of the left column and the start of the right).

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: all eight text lines on face 1 (there is nothing else). Unread: the covered stretches of lines 3-4; face 2 (blank/ruled as exposed). Tiles: image-004 = left part of left column; image-003 = right part of left column + start of right column (overlaps both neighbours); image-002 = right part of right column. Overlapping words are given once.

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE 1 (images 002-004)

Left column (lines numbered from top of tile; image-004 for the line beginnings, image-003 for the line ends)

image-004/003 line 1:  [..]truwet daz ich(?) mit(?) an betruwet si . W' (W[er]? / W[ir]?) ist
image-004/003 line 2:  [covered] an [ge?]lowwen od' (od[er]) an kein' (kein[er]) tugent mit
image-004/003 line 3:  [covered] also(?) le[..]en(?) [covered] als vm(?) mich(?) sollen(?) [end partly covered]
image-004/003 line 4:  S(?)[covered]nd(?)unge gege[covered]n ei(?) im(?) vergevnte(?)

Notes, left column:
- line 1: first word begins in the torn area; "-truwet" is clear, what precedes is lost. "ich" is written with a tall final letter (could be read "ih"/"ich"). The final word after the punctus is a W with a superscript sign followed by "ist"; expansion not certain.
- line 2: "[..]lowwen" - one or two letters before "lowwen" are under paper fibre; "ge-" is a guess from the space, hence the question mark.
- line 3: heavily covered; "als vm" (or "vin"/"vni") and a word with long s + ll ("sollen"?) are partly visible. A black blot sits over the middle of the line.
- line 4: an initial large curved stroke (S?) at the far left; "-nduge" with a stroke above (-ndunge?) ; "gege[..]n" ; last word begins "verg" or "vege" and ends "-vnte"/"-vute"; minims ambiguous.

Right column (image-003 for line beginnings, image-002 for the rest)

image-003/002 line 1:  meze . Wene(?) s . Paul' (Paul[us]) sp'ch' (sp[ri]ch[et]) [l?]i[.]et(?) ein gelit vn
image-003/002 line 2:  gemach die and'n (and[er]n) miteliten alle . also zwiual
image-003/002 line 3:  [covered]uu[.]z(?) an[covered]elu[covered] d' (d[er]) [..]s o[covered]
image-003/002 line 4:  [covered]al . daz ein[covered] stetig(?)[..]ge(?) and' (and[er]) waren

Notes, right column:
- line 1: "Wene" has a stroke over the first e (W[e]nne?). Between "sp'ch'" and "ein" is a word of about five letters, smudged; first letter tall (l or h), ends "-et"/"-ez"; I cannot settle it. "gelit vn" ends the line; a stroke may stand over "vn".
- line 2: "gemach" then a dark smudge, then "die"; "mitelitenalle" is written closely, word division mine. After the punctus "also" (damaged in the middle) and "zwiual" at line end (zwiual / zwiuel; the vowel before l looks like a).
- line 3: mostly under paper. Only isolated letters are seen.
- line 4: "stet-" or "sten-" followed by a damaged group ending "-ge"; I see a long s, t, e, then minims; "and' waren" at the end is fairly clear ("waren" could be "wazen"; r preferred).

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE 2 (images 005-008)
No text legible. Ruled lines only; scattered dark specks at image-008 (centre-right) and image-007 (right of centre) are not resolvable. If this is the other side of the same strip, its text is either on the glued-down side or abraded away.

LIMITATIONS
- Four lines per column only; the strip is cut so that line 1 is intact but anything above and below is lost.
- Lines 3 and 4 are fragmentary because of adhering paper; readings there are low confidence.
- Minim groups (m/n/u/i) are ambiguous throughout; no dots on i.
- Column order assumed left then right; the two columns are not textually continuous on this strip.
- Suggested further views: raking-light or UV of lines 3-4 of both columns; the glued side of the face-2 strip if it can be imaged by transmitted light.
